differential: Viral hepatitis
Acute viral infection is a very common cause of hepatocellular inflammation leading to jaundice and dark urine.
Alcoholic hepatitis
Significant alcohol consumption can cause acute liver injury and jaundice, which is a frequent presentation in this age group.
Drug-induced liver injury (DILI)
Many medications, supplements, or toxins can cause hepatocellular damage resulting in jaundice.
Choledocholithiasis
Obstruction of the common bile duct by a gallstone leads to cholestatic jaundice and dark urine.
Autoimmune hepatitis
Immune-mediated inflammation of the liver can present acutely with jaundice and is a consideration in young to middle-aged adults.
eliminated: Gilbert's syndrome
This condition causes a mild unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia and would not cause dark urine from bilirubinuria.
Hemolytic anemia
This causes an unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia due to red blood cell breakdown and does not cause bilirubinuria.

differential: Acute viral hepatitis

Choledocholithiasis

Autoimmune hepatitis

This is a cause of chronic cholestatic jaundice that typically affects young to middle-aged men.
